Concurrency & Isolation Modes

1. Concurrency Modes
ModeDescription
PESSIMISTIC Locks are acquired immediately when a key is first accessed within the transaction; other transactions that try to access the same key are blocked until the lock is released;
OPTIMISTIC No locks are acquired during the transaction; locks are only acquired at commit time; if another transaction modified the same key, the commit fails with a conflict exception;
2. Isolation Levels
LevelDescription
READ_COMMITTED A transaction reads the latest committed value; two reads of the same key may return different values if another transaction committed in between;
REPEATABLE_READ Once a key is read, subsequent reads within the same transaction return the same value;
SERIALIZABLE Transactions behave as if they executed one at a time (fully serial); highest isolation but lowest concurrency;
3. Valid Combinations
ConcurrencyIsolationBehavior
PESSIMISTIC READ_COMMITTED Lock on first access; reads see latest committed value
PESSIMISTIC REPEATABLE_READ Lock on first access; reads are consistent within the transaction
PESSIMISTIC SERIALIZABLE Same as PESSIMISTIC + REPEATABLE_READ in practice
OPTIMISTIC READ_COMMITTED No locks until commit; no conflict detection
OPTIMISTIC REPEATABLE_READ No locks until commit; conflict detection at commit time
OPTIMISTIC SERIALIZABLE No locks until commit; full conflict detection (strongest)
4. Choosing a Mode
  • PESSIMISTIC + REPEATABLE_READ — safest and most predictable; use for most transactional workloads;
  • OPTIMISTIC + SERIALIZABLE — highest concurrency but transactions may fail on commit and need retry logic; good when conflicts are rare;
  • OPTIMISTIC + READ_COMMITTED — lightweight but no conflict detection; use only when you can tolerate stale reads;
5. Default Transaction Settings
  • Configure defaults so you don't have to specify them on every transaction: 
    TransactionConfiguration txCfg = new TransactionConfiguration();
txCfg.setDefaultTxConcurrency(TransactionConcurrency.PESSIMISTIC);
txCfg.setDefaultTxIsolation(TransactionIsolation.REPEATABLE_READ);
txCfg.setDefaultTxTimeout(10_000);

IgniteConfiguration igniteCfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
igniteCfg.setTransactionConfiguration(txCfg);
